Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: We need to log foods. The user says they had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We should log each item. For each log_food call we need to provide food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We can assume default meal_type snack? But maybe we can specify meal_type based on context: first mention might be breakfast? They didn't specify times. We could ask clarifying question but likely we just log them. Use portion_unit: piece for mango? They said pieces. So portion_unit "piece". Portion_amount 8. Food_name "frozen mango"? Or "mango"? Probably "frozen mango". Meal_type maybe "snack" default. Log_date default null. Next: chai tea: portion_amount 1? Unit "cup"? They didn't specify quantity. Could assume 1 cup. Food_name "chai tea". Portion_unit "cup". Next: pepperoni pizza slices: portion_amount 2, portion_unit "slice", food_name "pepperoni pizza". Next: coffee: portion_amount 1, portion_unit "cup". Let's log each. We'll produce separate calls.
